newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.5 pct on minor cash entry.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.5 pct on minor cash entry.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted gains in continued technical rebound on Wednesday with the help of limited cash entry, but the upside was seen capped due to firm resistance at the index's 65,000 level, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed 974.22 points, or 1.53 percent higher at 64,616.63. Trade volume leapt further to 8.91 trillion lira ($100.3 million) from Tuesday's 6.12 trillion ($69.1 million).
Brokers said selling sparked by news that Iraqi forces fired one or two anti-aircraft missiles at U.S. fighter jets over northern Iraq was quickly overcome by selective purchases.
"If cash influx continues, the 65,000-65,500 barrier may be tested this week. Privatisation news also helped to move the market," said Huseyin Istanbullu from Meksa securities.

State Minister Ufuk Soylemez said the privatisation agency OIB would draw up and announce next week a sell-off calendar for 1996 and coming years. His statements kept activity focused on shares of largely state owned companies.
The government is seeking ways of speeding up sell-offs to close big state deficits.
The market began a recovery after support of the index was confirmed at 62,500 on Monday when it eased 0.84 percent on top of last week's 1.7 percent loss.
